name: Blue/Blue Belly (2014 refresh)
description: White fuselage with a navy belly from the nose to behind the wing; 'jetBlue' in large navy lower case over the forward windows; navy engines with 'jetblue.com' in white; the fin in one of JetBlue's tail designs with 'jetBlue' in white on it. Drawn with Balloons, the A321 family's design (big overlapping discs in light, sky and dark blue on a mid-blue fin); Prism (JBU/prism) is drawn separately. The A320s carry a dozen other designs (Dots, Bubbles, Mosaic, Harlequin, Barcode, Highrise, Tartan, Blueberries, Stripes and more), spread across the fleet; those aren't drawn.

notes: Drawn from the A321neo N2017J (Dec 2025). The fin is drawn as Balloons, the commonest single tail (the A321neos and many A321ceos, Mint or not, on Commons photos from 2026): discs laid out on the fin as built, by eye from N2180J and N923JB, not traced; the real pattern's exact layout differs. An A320 in this scheme usually carries another design. Each aircraft also has a name ('Crème Bluelée' here) under the cockpit, not drawn. Re-checked 2026-11-15 for the A320 (JetBlue's commonest type): the title measured on N2017J in metres (starts 1.5 m behind the forward door's middle, 6.8 m long, cap height 1.57 m, its baseline about 0.47 m under the windows' bottom; lowercase 0.76 of the capitals) and placed on the A320's outline, checked against N627JB (A320); 'jetblue.com' on the A320's nacelle runs x 0.43-0.79 (N627JB, N615JB; on the A321neo's it is further forward, 0.14-0.64). The fin title is larger than first drawn: baseline at 0.18 of the fin, cap 0.16, x 0.31-0.84 of the chord on both types. On the A321 the title covers a smaller share (x 0.137-0.290).
history: Replaces Skyarium v1's approximate standard (a few colors from memory). The 2014 refresh added the navy belly and 'jetblue.com' engines to the 2000 white-and-blue tail design scheme.
